svg.text: Four ways a herbal remedy causes harm
Natural describes the origin, not the safety
1. Delay
Weeks of treatment at home while the disease advances
The child with malaria who arrives convulsing
The breast lump that was small a year ago
The fracture splinted tightly until the limb dies
This is the biggest harm, and it is invisible
in the product, because the product did nothing
Ask how long, not only what
2. Interaction
Plants contain active chemicals, so they behave
like drugs and interact like drugs
Bleeding risk with an anticoagulant
Unpredictable glucose with a diabetes medicine
Lowered levels of antiretroviral or antiepileptic drugs
The interaction is invisible unless you asked
Treatment failure is sometimes an interaction, not resistance
3. Direct toxicity
Liver injury: jaundice, dark urine, nausea, itching
Kidney injury: falling urine output, swelling
Harsh purgatives and enemas: fluid and potassium loss,
dangerous in a small child or a frail older person
Corrosive applications to the eye, the cord, the skin
A plant that acts on the body can injure the body
Unexplained jaundice or renal failure: ask what she
has been drinking, and ask more than once
4. What is actually in the bottle
Dose varies from batch to batch and season to season
Preparations mix several plants, unnamed
Some are adulterated with hidden orthodox drugs,
most often steroids or painkillers
Some carry heavy metals or contaminated water
A registered product has been assessed for this;
a roadside mixture has not
Sudden relief followed by a moon face suggests
a steroid nobody declared
